page: Amazon Web Services c8a.large is a compute-optimized server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9R45 processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs, operating at a high clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The instance is equipped with 4.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory running at 6 GHz, yielding a compute-focused allocation of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It utilizes the AWS Nitro hypervisor and does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware. Network connectivity is established with a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core capabilities, with the stress-ng single-core CPU performance, Geekbench single-core score, and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression all placing in the top tier. However, multi-core and multi-threaded performance metrics, such as the Geekbench multi-core score and stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, fall into the average category. The instance exhibits weaker performance in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, software compilation with Clang, and Passmark memory scores, which rank in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth remains average, with read-only small block cached transfers reaching 430.39 GB/sec and large block uncached writes at 34.83 GB/sec.

The c8a.large offers a highly cost-efficient profile for workloads requiring intense single-threaded processing power without the overhead of high memory capacity. The dedicated CPU allocation and 4.5 GHz clock speed provide predictable performance for compute-bound tasks. However, the 4.0 GB RAM limit and lack of local storage represent significant tradeoffs, making this instance less suitable for memory-heavy databases or large-scale parallel compilation. It is best suited for lightweight web serving, single-threaded data processing, text processing, and low-intensity Redis deployments.
